brief.analysis: The strongest regime argument is a genuine multi-year structural shift: NATO's Hague commitment to 5% of GDP by 2035 (3.5% core) plus ~20% 2025 European spending growth is lifting the defense mean itself, not just its price. This is confirmed directly in the data — detrended z is -0.17 versus raw +1.12, a divergence of more than a sigma showing the ratio sits below its own rising trend even while above the flat mean, so the mean is drifting up. With the 200DMA already achieved, a weak 3/6 base rate and slope not confirmed, shorting toward the -11.9% flat 5-year mean is shorting into a rising structural trend; that target is a trap.
brief.report_line: Short ITA/SPY should be avoided: with detrended z at -0.17 versus raw +1.12 the ratio is below its own rising trend, and NATO's 5%-of-GDP rearmament path has moved the defense mean up, so the flat 5-year-mean target is statistically invalid.

brief.analysis: The strongest regime argument is a durable secular index-share gain: the AI capex cycle is still extending, with leading-edge capacity expected tight into 2027-2028, so semis' rise versus the Nasdaq reflects structural earnings power, not a temporary dislocation. Raw and detrended z agree at ~3.0 and 50DMA slope is still intact against the short, meaning nothing has broken the uptrend yet. The +75% pull to the flat 5-year mean assumes semis surrender a decade of AI-driven weight gains and is an invalid target; only the +20.6% 200DMA target is defensible, and even that is a fade, not a reversion.
brief.report_line: Short SMH/QQQ (3.1z) is a WL fade toward the 200DMA at best; the 5-year-mean target is invalid because the AI capex cycle has structurally raised semis' index share, so treat any short as a tactical trim, not a reversion trade.

brief.analysis: The regime case is real: silver's ~147% 2025 run was driven by a multiyear structural supply deficit, ETP inflows and even first-ever sovereign reserve inclusion, which can hold the ratio structurally higher than its flat 5-year mean. But the extreme has already worked itself off — peak z of 6.36 has collapsed to 1.07, the 200DMA target is achieved, 3/3 MA confirmation and the 50DMA has turned — so the dislocation is largely spent rather than fresh. The 200DMA has been reached and the flat +14.8% mean target is aggressive against a metal whose own uptrend is still intact; size down and treat the 5-year mean as a stretch, not a base case.
brief.report_line: Short SLV/GLD is HC and MA-confirmed but the z-score has already normalized to 1.07 with the 200DMA hit; the residual +14.8% to the 5-year mean fights silver's intact structural deficit, so size down and anchor on the 200DMA, not the flat mean.
